spec.name: krsm-2rot-v1
spec.limitations: Not a secure cipher. The only cross-byte diffusion is two whole-buffer rotations (5 and 11) around forward-causal running sums, so an attacker can guess a rotation offset and peel bytes from the buffer ends; the 128-bit key repeats with period 16, so short messages expose few independent key bytes per position, and single-byte chosen-plaintext differences can be traced through the mod-256 sums. Both rotations act as the identity if the message length is 5 or 11, and buffers of length 1-2 leave the construction essentially byte-local.
spec.math: On Z_256^L: S(x)_i = x_i xor k_i; D(x)_i = (x_i + k_i) mod 256; R_r = left rotate each byte by r bits; C(x)_i = sum_{j=0..i} x_j mod 256, with inverse C^-1(x)_i = x_i - x_{i-1} mod 256 (x_{-1}=0); P_n = cyclic left shift of the whole buffer by n positions, inverse P_{L - n mod L}; X_c(x)_i = x_i xor c; A_c(x)_i = (x_i + c) mod 256. Every step is a bijection of Z_256^L (inverses S, D_{256-k}, R_{8-r}, P^-1, X_c, A_{256-c}), so the 12-step composition is exactly invertible. Addition appears twice (add_key and chain_add); keyed steps appear twice (xor_key and add_key), so the key space is the full 128 bits.
spec.assumptions: Known- or chosen-plaintext attack model against a fixed uniformly random 16-byte key with round-robin reuse; buffer length L >= 3 and L not in {5,11} so both rotations are non-identity; every operand as written is in 0..255.
